items.stem: A weight lifter lifts a barbell as shown in the figure . List two forces that are acting on the barbell. Are these forces balanced if the weight lifter keeps the barbell steady?
items.answer: The two primary forces acting on the barbell are the downward gravitational force exerted by the Earth and the upward force applied by the weightlifter’s hands. Yes, if the weightlifter keeps the barbell completely steady, these two opposing forces are equal in magnitude and are balanced.

(b) Sublimation is the process where a solid changes directly into the vapour state on heating (or at room temperature for some volatile substances) without passing through the liquid state. (c) He could put the mixture in a china dish with an inverted funnel plugged with cotton over it, and heat it gently. The naphthalene would sublime and form solid deposits on the inner walls of the funnel, leaving the sand behind. (d) Solid carbon dioxide, also known as dry ice, undergoes sublimation. items.stem: A forensics student is investigating a case of a forged signature on a cheque. The suspect claims the signature was written using a standard black sketch pen found in the office. The student decides to test the ink. She places a tiny spot of ink from the cheque onto a thin strip of specialized filter paper. She carefully suspends the paper in a beaker containing a small amount of water, ensuring the ink spot sits just above the water level. After twenty minutes, she observes a beautiful band of blue, yellow, and red streaks climbing up the paper. QUESTIONS: (a) Identify the scientific technique being used by the forensics student to analyze the ink. (b) What can the student infer about the black ink based on the coloured streaks on the paper? (c) Explain the basic principle that allows the different colours to separate on the paper. (d) Why was it crucial for the student to keep the ink spot slightly above the water level at the beginning of the experiment?
items.answer: (a) The technique is paper chromatography. (b) The student can infer that the black ink is not a single pure substance, but a homogeneous mixture of multiple coloured components (dyes). (c) The separation is based on differences in the interactions of the components with the solvent and the paper. As the solvent (water) rises, it carries the dyes with it at different speeds, separating them. (d) If the ink spot was submerged in the water, the ink would simply dissolve into the bulk of the water at the bottom of the beaker instead of travelling up the paper strip.

items.stem: During a practical exam, a student accidentally pours acetone into a flask that contains pure distilled water. Acetone is highly miscible in water, resulting in a perfectly clear mixture. The teacher informs the student that the boiling point of water is 100 °C, while the boiling point of acetone is much lower, at 56 °C. She challenges the student to set up an apparatus to recover both liquids in their pure forms without losing either to the atmosphere. QUESTIONS: (a) Name the process the student should use to separate this mixture of miscible liquids. (b) Why is this specific separation process effective for the acetone and water mixture? (c) As the mixture is heated, which liquid will turn into vapour first, and why? (d) What is the role of the water condenser in this apparatus? (e) If the student had mixed two liquids with boiling points of 75 °C and 78 °C, could this exact same simple setup be used effectively? Explain.
items.answer: (a) The student should use the distillation process. (b) Distillation is effective because acetone and water are miscible liquids that boil without decomposition and have a sufficient difference in their boiling points (greater than 25 °C). (c) Acetone will vaporize first because it has a lower boiling point (56 °C) compared to water (100 °C). (d) The condenser cools the hot vapours of the vaporized liquid (acetone) by circulating cold water around it, turning the vapour back into a liquid so it can be collected in a separate flask. (e) No, simple distillation would not be effective because the difference in boiling points is less than 25 °C.
